title: Peer Review Auditing and Evaluation Protocol
author: Paola Di Maio

steps.title: Publish Evaluation Criteria
steps.instruction: Publish the complete evaluation criteria for assessing submissions, ensuring they are publicly accessible before the submission deadline.

substeps.instruction: Record the URL of the published criteria document, date of publication, and version number.
Ensure the document lists all evaluation dimensions, scoring scales, and acceptance thresholds.

steps.title: Register AI Tools
steps.instruction: Document every AI tool used in the assessment pipeline (e.g., LLM detectors, plagiarism checkers, statistical screeners, automated formatters, scope classifiers) using a Digital Forensics Model Card (DF-MC).

substeps.instruction: Use the generator at https://huggingface.co/spaces/STARBORN/forensics_mc_generator to create the DF-MC.

Record for each tool: name and version, forensic domain classification, reasoning type (deductive, inductive, abductive, hybrid), known bias types/causes, known error types/causes (especially false positive rates), forensic process stages involved, whether human review is required, and known limitations (language coverage, text length sensitivity, adversarial vulnerabilities).
Save the resulting JSON output in the venue’s DF-MC Registry.

steps.title: Configure Conflict of Interest Policy
steps.instruction: Document the conflict of interest (COI) criteria for reviewer assignment.

substeps.instruction: Specify co-authorship lookback period (e.g., 3 years, 5 years), institutional affiliation conflicts, funding source conflicts, and personal relationship declarations.
Specify whether COI checks are automated, manual, or both.
Record the COI policy document, date of adoption, and method of enforcement.

steps.title: Configure Appeal Pathway
steps.instruction: Document the appeal process and make it accessible to submitters.

substeps.instruction: Define eligibility criteria for appeals and the timeline for filing.
Define how appeal reviewers are assigned (ensuring they were not original decision-makers).
Define how outcomes are communicated and whether aggregate statistics will be published.
Record the appeal policy document and date of adoption.

steps.title: Receive and Timestamp Submissions
steps.instruction: Upon receipt of each submission, generate a Layer 1 audit record.

substeps.instruction: Generate a unique submission identifier.
Generate a cryptographic timestamp in ISO 8601 format.
Perform a completeness check confirmation.
Perform an anonymisation verification (for double-blind venues).
Ensure all Layer 1 metadata is accessible to the submitting author in real time.

steps.title: Run AI Tools and Log Invocations
steps.instruction: Log every invocation of an AI tool on a submission.

substeps.instruction: Record tool identifier and version (linking to the DF-MC registry).
Record timestamp of invocation.
Record input hash (cryptographic hash preserving confidentiality, not the content).
Record output classification (e.g., “human-authored”, “AI-flagged”, “clear”, “suspicious”).
Record confidence score and the decision threshold applied.
Record whether the output was reviewed by a human before action was taken.

steps.title: Record Desk Rejections
steps.instruction: If a submission is desk-rejected, create a Layer 1 desk rejection record.

substeps.instruction: Record the timestamp of the decision.
Assign a coded reason from a published taxonomy (e.g., “out-of-scope”, “formatting-non-compliant”, “duplicate-submission”, “integrity-flag”, “capacity-constraint”).
Record whether any AI tool output contributed to the decision.
Record the identity of the human decision-maker (pseudonymised).

steps.title: Assign Reviewers and Log Metadata
steps.instruction: Assign reviewers and record Layer 2 metadata.

substeps.instruction: Record the number of reviewers assigned and the timestamp of assignment.
Confirm COI checks were performed per policy and record the method (automated, manual, or both).
Record any reassignments with coded reasons.

steps.title: Monitor Review Completion
steps.instruction: Record Layer 3 metadata for each assigned reviewer using pseudonymous identifiers (e.g., Reviewer-A).

substeps.instruction: Record timestamp of assignment acceptance and review submission.
Perform a structural completeness check to see if the review addresses all required evaluation criteria.
Record word count, whether actionable feedback is provided, and whether the review engages with the methodology.
Record timeline compliance regarding the venue's stated deadline.

steps.title: Record the Decision
steps.instruction: Record the final editorial, panel, or committee decision as Layer 4 metadata.

substeps.instruction: Record timestamp and outcome (accept, minor-revision, major-revision, reject, desk-reject, withdrawn).
Record how individual scores mapped to the final decision and if it was consistent with the aggregate reviewer recommendation.
If the decision overrode the aggregate recommendation, record a coded justification (editorial-judgment, scope-mismatch, integrity-concern, capacity-constraint, other).
Record any use of editorial override and whether minority reviewer opinions were noted.

steps.title: Collect Aggregated Demographics
steps.instruction: Compile aggregated demographic data at the decision stage for fairness analysis, applying differential privacy techniques for small sample sizes.

substeps.instruction: Calculate acceptance rates and desk rejection rates by author region, career stage, institution type, and language background.
Calculate AI tool flag rates by the same categories.
Ensure only aggregated statistics are recorded, never individual-level data.

steps.title: Process Appeals
steps.instruction: If a decision is appealed, record Layer 5 metadata.

substeps.instruction: Record the appeal filing timestamp.
Confirm the appeal reviewer was not involved in the original decision.
Record the appeal outcome with a coded reason.
Record the timeline from filing to resolution.

steps.title: Generate Review Process Model Card
steps.instruction: Generate a Review Process Model Card (JSON) for each submission that completed the review cycle using the OAMAP generator at rpmc-seven.vercel.app.

substeps.instruction: Summarize Layers 0-5 into the structured document.
Store the JSON model card in the venue’s audit archive.

steps.title: Produce Venue-Level Compliance Report
steps.instruction: Produce a venue-level OAMAP compliance report at the end of each review cycle.

substeps.instruction: Include: total submissions, desk rejection rate (by coded reason), average reviewers per submission, timeline adherence rate, criteria coverage rate, decision-score consistency rate, override rate (by coded reason), appeal rate/outcomes, aggregated fairness statistics, and AI tool invocation summary (tools used, flag rates, false positive estimates).
Publish the report or make it available to authorised auditors.
